introduction: On this seventh Sunday of Easter, between the Ascension and Pentecost, we hear Jesus pray at the Last Supper for all who will believe through the apostles' word: that they may all be one. Stephen, the first martyr, sees heaven opened and forgives those who stone him. The Book of Revelation ends with the cry, Come, Lord Jesus. Let us pray with Jesus for the unity of his Church, and for the coming of the Spirit.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, Jesus prayed for us, that we may all be one. Let us join our prayers to his.
intentions: For the unity of all Christians: that we may be one, as the Father and the Son are one, so that the world may believe. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who are persecuted and martyred for their faith: that, like Saint Stephen, they may be filled with the Holy Spirit. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who have wronged us: that we may forgive them, as Stephen forgave his persecutors. Let us pray to the Lord.
For all who are preparing for Confirmation: that they may receive the Holy Spirit with open hearts. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that we may long for the coming of Christ and pray each day, Come, Lord Jesus. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: Holy Father, your Son prayed that all who believe in him may be one. Hear his prayer and ours, and send us your Holy Spirit to make us one in love. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: That they may all be one
reflection.body:
On the night before he died, Jesus prayed for his disciples. Today's Gospel shows that he also prayed for us: "Not for these only do I pray, but for those also who will believe in me through their word." Every Christian who has ever believed was in his heart that night.

What did he ask for? Unity: "that they may all be one; even as you, Father, are in me, and I in you." The unity of Christians is to reflect the unity of the Father and the Son. And it has a purpose: "that the world may believe that you sent me." Divisions among Christians make it harder for the world to believe.

Jesus also prays that we may be with him: "Father, I desire that they also whom you have given me be with me where I am, that they may see my glory." And he prays that God's own love may live in us: "that the love with which you loved me may be in them, and I in them."

The first reading shows what this love looks like under pressure. Stephen, the first Christian martyr, is stoned for his faith. He sees heaven opened and Jesus standing at the right hand of God. As he dies, he prays as Jesus did on the cross: "Lord Jesus, receive my spirit!" and "Lord, don't hold this sin against them!" A young man named Saul watches. He will later become Saint Paul.

The Book of Revelation ends with a longing: "The Spirit and the bride say," Come! And it closes with the prayer, "Yes, come, Lord Jesus!"

In these days before Pentecost, pray each day for the unity of Christians, and for the gift of the Holy Spirit. And if there is someone you need to forgive, ask Stephen to help you.
